subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — deployment mode + geo gating for PoC
messages:
From: Anil Sharma <anil@medibridge.com>

Cc: MediBridge Procurement <procurement@medibridge.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP ask & geo question

Evelyn — thanks again for the demo today. Procurement asked that we capture a short mutual action plan for the PoC and make the hosting decision explicit up front (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Two quick asks from our side: 1) can you sketch the MAP milestones with a gate that decides deployment mode, and 2) what timelines do you need for the US-only region given our PHI constraints?

We're trying to lock the procurement cycle (legal + security) by mid-August so any clear gating criteria would help.

Cheers,
Anil
Head of Platform Engineering, MediBridge
(anil@medibridge.com)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask & geo question

Thanks Anil — appreciate the clear asks. I've attached a first-pass MAP and a security evidence bundle for your reviewers (see attachments). High level proposal here so procurement and security can align quickly: 

- MAP milestones (PoC scope): discovery (1 week), integration sprint (2 weeks), perf & cost eval (1 week), security review (concurrent), go/no-go gate for deployment mode decision (end of week 4).
- Deployment-mode gate: we propose a small decision matrix — if PHI-in-scope and customer requires on-prem or VPC isolation -> Private; if throughput > 2M tokens/day with steady low latency SLO (<50ms) and dedicated budget -> Dedicated; otherwise choose Hosted for fastest time-to-value.
- Geo gating: default to US region (primary) with failover to east/west multi-zone. If regulated-data residency required, mark as US-only region; that triggers a 2-week additional compliance window for Private or Dedicated in-region provisioning.

Action items for MediBridge to unblock the gate: confirm PHI scope, share expected avg/peak token volumes, and indicate whether their legal team needs a dedicated contract (vs standard TOS). Once we have that, we can commit the PoC calendar and estimate costs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

I've included the MAP doc: 20270801-MediBridge-MAP-v1.pdf and a short evidence zip for SOC2 items.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
T: +1 415-555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + decision matrix (technical notes)

Eve — copied my quick technical read and a recommendation for the gate mechanics. Quoting your map below: 

> "if throughput > 2M tokens/day with steady low latency SLO (<50ms) and dedicated budget -> Dedicated"

Notes: 
- The throughput break should be driven by cost/latency tradeoffs. For the PoC we recommend measuring tokens/day and 95th pct latency during the integration sprint; if 95th pct > 80ms on Hosted with our default batching, the economics favor Dedicated because it removes noisy neighbors and enables reserved kernels/quantization profiles.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) will add a 2–4 week provisioning window for infra + security attestation; include that in the MAP as an explicit dependency so procurement can see the timeline impact.
- Region selection: if MediBridge requires US-only data residency, we propose using us-west for lower latency to the customer's primary DC and us-east for DR. Kicking a region-only decision to legal/security should be part of the gate checklist.

Suggested gate checklist items (tech): expected token profile (avg/95th/peak), latency SLO target, list of external integrations (EHR connectors), and whether KMS/HSM is required for key control. If any item is unresolved at gate, fallback policy = Hosted with strict SLA and an automatic re-eval at week 8.

I'll add rough cost deltas for Hosted vs Dedicated (PoC) into the MAP doc and push a v1.1 later today.

—Karthik
Principal Backend Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP checkpoint — deployment mode + geo gating for PoC

Anil — quick note from the account team on procurement timing: if MediBridge can confirm PHI scope and sign the mutual NDA by Aug 9, we can commit to the proposed PoC start (week of Aug 16). For Dedicated or Private we will need a one-week uplift on lead time for capacity scheduling (Dedicated) or a 2–4 week provisioning window (Private).

Linking HubSpot deal for transparency: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/123456/DEAL-9872 — I put the procurement milestone and legal contacts there. Once you confirm the PHI scope and expected token load we'll attach the cost scenarios and a targeted SOW.

Next steps I propose: MediBridge confirms PHI scope (reply inline), then Redwood will produce a v1.1 MAP with cost scenarios for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private by EOD Aug 2. We'll also surface the minimum security evidence package needed for your security review.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — confirmed: PHI will be in-scope for the PoC (summary PII + limited PHI fragments). Token profile rough estimate: avg ~150k tokens/day, peak bursts ~1.2M tokens/day during batch processing windows. Procurement will sign the NDA by Aug 6.

We'd prefer Dedicated if the cost delta vs Hosted is within 30% and the latency variance improves at the 95th pct. If Dedicated looks >30% more expensive, we'll evaluate Private but need a detailed compliance checklist for that path. Please send the v1.1 MAP and cost scenarios.

Anil
